Subject: Commercial proposal: rebate vs prepaid structure & implementation timeline

Hi Vivek / team,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We received the internal RFP follow-up and want to evaluate two commercial constructs from Redwood: a volume-anchored rebate (paid retro based on run-rate) vs an upfront/prepaid credit (discounted buy-down).

Attached is the formal RFP extract and our procurement constraints. High level asks:
- Clear unit economics (effective discount / $ per inference) for both constructs over 12 and 24 month horizons
- Any onboarding/implementation credits baked into the offer and timing of those credits
- Minimum commit or term required to qualify for the rebate or prepay discount
- Typical DocuSign timeline and implementation kickoff availability

Can you send a short proposal (1-2 pages) outlining both options and a recommended path? We aim to present to finance this Thursday.

Attachment: MapleHealth_RFP.xlsx (spreadsheet, 145KB)

Best,
John Carter
Procurement Manager
MapleHealth

John — thanks for the RFP snippet. We can do both constructs; high-level here and I will follow up with a short attachment that breaks the numbers into 12/24 month scenarios. Quick summary (will formalize in the attached spreadsheet):

Option 1 — Volume-anchored rebate:
- Annualized rebate computed on net monthly consumption vs committed baseline
- Typical rebate band: 3.5% — 8% effective depending on committed run-rate and multiyear term
- Rebate paid quarterly, requires 12-month min term; 24-month term improves rates and can include performance SLAs
- Implementation credit: one-time onboarding credit applied to first invoice (usually 10–25% of first-month run-rate; can be structured as a credit bucket)

Option 2 — Upfront prepaid credit:
- Prepaid balance purchased at a discount (typical 5–12% depending on upfront amount) and drawn down as consumed
- Onboarding credit: smaller (we offset with more generous prepay discount) or can be combined with waived professional services for first 30 days
- No retro rebates; pricing during drawdown fixed to the prepaid discount tiers

Key negotiation levers we can use: minimum term, onboarding credit size, SLA credit threshold, and tiered discounts for seat/throughput commitments.

I attached an initial economics workbook for your review — includes modeled examples at your reported monthly token volumes. I’m available for a 30-minute call tomorrow 10–10:30am PT or Wednesday 2–3pm PT to walk finance through the options.

Attachment: redwood-initial-econ.xlsx (spreadsheet, 88KB)

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek — looping internal stakeholders and drafting negotiation guardrails.

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 4:30 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Key negotiation levers we can use: minimum term, onboarding credit size, SLA credit threshold, and tiered discounts for seat/throughput commitments.

Notes / suggested stance:
- Goal: preserve gross margin while keeping effective customer TCO within competitive window. Avoid giving both a large prepay discount and a sizable onboarding credit unless we tie to a commit.
- Anchor offer: 12-month term, performance SLA (p99 latency SLA for critical routes), 6% effective rebate at target V1 run-rate. Implementation credit = one-time credit equal to 20% of first-month run-rate (applied within first invoice). This is our reference offer.
- Trade-off: If customer requests a full upfront prepay discount we can increase discount to 9–10% but require a 6-month minimum non-refundable drawdown and reduce onboarding credit to 5–10%.
- Upsell kicker: include a staged price step-down at 12 months for committed growth >20% YOY.

Questions for sign-off:
1) Can we commit to a 20% onboarding credit at the reference offer? (Marissa — ops impact / accounting treatment?)
2) Connor — confirm legal ok with the tiered rebate language (quarterly true-up, subject to audit clause).

If we agree, I’ll fold into the customer-facing amendment and send for signatures.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Programs, Redwood Inference

John / Olivia — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Per our call earlier this week, here are two executable options. I’ve attached a short amendment (redwood-draft-amendment-v2.pdf) and a polished RFP response. If either option fits, we can route via DocuSign and schedule implementation kickoff within 5 business days of signature.

Option A — Anchored rebate (Reference Offer)
- Term: 12 months
- Commit baseline: X monthly tokens (see attachment spreadsheet for the exact #s)
- Effective rebate: 6% on net consumption above baseline (true-up quarterly)
- Implementation credit: one-time 20% credit of the first-month run-rate, applied to first invoice
- SLA: p99 latency target, credit threshold applies beyond two breaches per quarter
- DocuSign turnaround: estimated 48–72 hours after countersignature

Option B — Prepaid credit (Upfront Buy-down)
- Term: prepaid balance drawn down over 12 months (minimum 6-month non-refundable drawdown)
- Prepay discount: 9% on purchased balance (higher discounts available at larger prepay buckets)
- Implementation credit: 7% of estimated first-month run-rate (lower than Option A in exchange for higher prepay discount)
- No quarterly rebate true-up (pricing fixed during drawdown)

Recommended next steps:
1) Choose Option A or B and confirm baseline run-rate (we used the numbers from your RFP for the attachment).
2) I will send redwood-draft-amendment-v2.pdf to your DocuSign with a 5-day expiration. Please review change-tracking in the PDF for legal-friendly redlines.
3) Kickoff: PM assigns onboarding resources and schedule within 5 business days of DocuSign completion.

Attachments: redwood-draft-amendment-v2.pdf (proposal amendment, 120KB); MapleHealth_RFP_response.pdf (RFP response, 260KB)

DocuSign (if helpful): https://docusign.com/embedded?token=abc123-maple
